question.problem: An angle $\theta $ in the coordinate plane (measured in the usual way) has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{7}.$ Which of the following cannot be $\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's remind ourselves of the relationship between ${\theta }_{R}$ and $\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/35e9a04cf71b42acdf7769ef541c5b93c9267130e965d52d3989f3a00692cea1.png)

Using ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{7},$ let's calculate all possible values of $\theta .$

- If $\theta $ lies in the first quadrant, then $\theta ={\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{7}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the second quadrant, then $\theta =\pi -{\theta }_{R}=\pi -\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{6\pi }{7}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the third quadrant, then $\theta =\pi +{\theta }_{R}=\pi +\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{8\pi }{7}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the fourth quadrant, then $\theta =2\pi -{\theta }_{R}=2\pi -\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{13\pi }{7}.$

Therefore, $\theta $ cannot be equal to $\frac{5\pi }{7}.$
